ba.why: 把 moves the object (门) before the verb.

ba.en: Where did you put your phone?
ba.why: 把 + object + verb + 在 + place: the verb has a result.
After 把 the verb needs a result or 了.
把 comes right before the object it moves.

bei.why: The fish is what was affected, so it comes first and 被 brings in the cat.

bei.en: A colleague has taken my notebook.
bei.why: Affected thing + 被 + who did it + verb + result.

bei.ch: 桌子上的西瓜被吃完了。
bei.en: The watermelon on the table has all been eaten.
bei.why: The doer can be left out: thing + 被 + verb + result still works.
After 被 the verb can't stand alone; it needs a result or 了, like 拿走了.

bei.en: My brother has gone off with my camera.
bei.why: 被 comes right after the thing affected, before the doer.

rang-cause.en: This whole thing makes me really angry.
rang-cause.why: When something causes a feeling, it's thing + 让 + person + feeling.

rang-cause.en: Mum was really pleased with these exam results.
rang-cause.why: The cause comes first, then 让 + who feels it + the feeling.
tpy: zhè cì kǎo shì de chéng jì

rang-cause.why: "Makes someone feel" is 让, never 做.

rang-cause.ch: 他突然离开，让大家都很担心。
rang-cause.en: His sudden departure had everyone worried.
rang-cause.why: The event comes first, then 让 + the people + how they feel.

rang-cause.en: The surroundings here make me feel at ease.
rang-cause.why: 让 goes between the cause and the person who feels it.

gen-yiyang.en: My birthday is the same as yours.
gen-yiyang.why: "The same as" is A 跟 B 一样.

gen-yiyang.en: This city isn't what it used to be.
gen-yiyang.why: A 跟 B, then 不 right before 一样.

gen-yiyang.ch: 他的汉语水平不跟我一样。
gen-yiyang.fix: 他的汉语水平跟我不一样。
gen-yiyang.en: His level of Chinese is different from mine.
gen-yiyang.why: 不 goes right before 一样, not before 跟.

gen-yiyang.ch: 你的裙子跟她的一样漂亮。
gen-yiyang.en: Your skirt is as pretty as hers.
gen-yiyang.why: A 跟 B 一样 + adjective means "as … as".

gen-yiyang.en: My son loves playing football, just like me.
gen-yiyang.why: 一样 comes after B and before the part that says in what way.

meiyou-bi.ch: 这家饭店的菜__那家好吃。
meiyou-bi.en: The food here isn't as good as at that restaurant.
meiyou-bi.why: A 没有 B + adjective: A doesn't come up to B.

meiyou-bi.en: My room isn't as big as yours.

meiyou-bi.ch: 这个苹果没有那个很甜。
meiyou-bi.en: This apple isn't as sweet as that one.
meiyou-bi.why: No 很 before the adjective in a 没有 comparison.

meiyou-bi.ch: 我做菜做得没有妈妈好。
meiyou-bi.en: I don't cook as well as Mum.
meiyou-bi.why: 没有 + B + adjective says I fall short of Mum.

meiyou-bi.en: This shirt isn't as cheap as that one.
meiyou-bi.why: 没有 goes between the two things being compared.

geng-hai.en: My little sister is even taller than me.
geng-hai.why: In a 比 sentence only 更 or 还 can go before the adjective.

geng-hai.en: This city is even bigger than Beijing.
geng-hai.why: A 比 B + 还 + adjective: B is big, A is even bigger.

geng-hai.ch: 这个房间比那个非常干净。
geng-hai.fix: 这个房间比那个更干净。
geng-hai.en: This room is even cleaner than that one.
geng-hai.why: 非常 can't go in a 比 sentence; use 更 or 还.

geng-hai.ch: 他的汉语说得比中国人还好。
geng-hai.en: He speaks Chinese even better than a Chinese person.
geng-hai.why: 还 before the adjective adds "even", with a note of surprise.

geng-hai.en: I think autumn is even nicer than summer.
geng-hai.why: 更 goes right before the adjective, after the 比 part.

zhe-exist.en: There's a cake sitting on the table.
zhe-exist.why: Place first, then verb + 着, then the thing.

zhe-exist.en: There are lots of old people sitting in the park.
zhe-exist.why: Place + 坐着 + how many + who.

zhe-exist.en: There are lots of people standing at the door.
zhe-exist.why: The place comes first; the thing or people come at the end.

zhe-exist.ch: 我家楼下住着一位老医生。
zhe-exist.en: An old doctor lives downstairs from us.
zhe-exist.why: Place + 住着 + a person says who lives there.

zhe-exist.en: There's a panda drawn on his shirt.
zhe-exist.why: 着 goes right after the verb: 画着.

zhe-manner.en: He said with a smile, "That's all right."
zhe-manner.why: The 着 verb says how he said it: 笑着说.

zhe-manner.en: Grandma likes to read sitting down.
zhe-manner.why: 坐着 comes first and says how she reads.

zhe-manner.en: She goes running with music on.
zhe-manner.why: 着 goes right after the first verb, before its object.

zhe-manner.ch: 妈妈带着礼物去看奶奶了。
zhe-manner.en: Mum took a present and went to see Grandma.
zhe-manner.why: 带着 is the background; 了 goes with the main action, 去看奶奶.

zhe-manner.en: Don't eat standing up, sit down.
zhe-manner.why: 着 goes right after the first verb: 站着吃.

you-you.en: This room is big and clean.
you-you.why: The pattern needs 又 before both words: 又大又干净.

you-you.ch: 这里的苹果又很甜又很便宜。
you-you.fix: 这里的苹果又甜又便宜。
you-you.en: The apples here are sweet and cheap.
My little sister is clever and cute.
you-you.why: Two good qualities stacked with 又……又…….

you-you.en: This shirt is cheap and looks good.
you-you.why: Each quality gets its own 又: 又便宜又好看.

you-you.ch: 这家饭店的服务员__热情又认真。
you-you.en: The waiters at this restaurant are friendly and careful.
you-you.why: 又……又…… stacks two descriptions; 一边 is for actions.

yibian.ch: 爷爷喜欢一边喝茶__看报纸。
yibian.en: Grandpa likes to read the paper while he drinks his tea.
yibian.why: Two actions at once: 一边 A 一边 B.

yibian.ch: 这个面包一边便宜一边好吃。
yibian.fix: 这个面包又便宜又好吃。
yibian.en: This bread is cheap and tasty.
yibian.why: 一边 is for actions; two descriptions take 又……又…….

yibian.ch: 妈妈一边做菜一边唱歌。
yibian.why: Two actions going on at the same time.

yibian.ch: 一边他走路，一边打电话。
yibian.fix: 他一边走路，一边打电话。
yibian.en: He talks on the phone as he walks.
yibian.why: The subject comes once, before the first 一边.

yibian.en: The children sing as they walk.
yibian.why: Each action gets its own 一边.

xian-ranhou.ch: 我们先吃东西，__去看电影。
xian-ranhou.en: Let's eat something first, then go to the film.
xian-ranhou.why: 再 marks the next step, one that's still to come.

xian-ranhou.en: Have a shower first, then go to bed.
xian-ranhou.why: 先 goes right before the first verb; 再 before the next.

xian-ranhou.ch: 我们先坐地铁，然后换公共汽车。
xian-ranhou.en: We'll take the underground first, then change to a bus.
xian-ranhou.why: 先 marks the first step; 然后 starts the next one.

xian-ranhou.ch: 昨天我先去了银行，再去了超市。
xian-ranhou.fix: 昨天我先去了银行，然后去了超市。
xian-ranhou.en: Yesterday I went to the bank first, then the supermarket.
xian-ranhou.why: For steps already done, use 然后, not 再.

xian-ranhou.en: Tomorrow we'll go to the airport first, then fly to Beijing.
xian-ranhou.why: 先 goes after the subject, right before the verb.
ppy: zuò fēi jī qù Běi jīng

yue.why: 越来越 goes straight to the adjective, with no 很 or 更.

yue.en: The more I eat this dish, the better it tastes.
yue.why: 越 + verb + 越 + adjective: the more you do it, the more so.

yue.ch: 这个城市越来越很漂亮了。
yue.fix: 这个城市越来越漂亮了。
yue.en: This city is getting more and more beautiful.
yue.why: 越 already means "more", so no 很 after it.

yue.en: The more I read this book, the more I want to read it.
yue.why: 越 A 越 B: the more A, the more B.

yue.en: More and more people are learning Chinese.
yue.why: 越来越 goes right before the adjective.
ppy: xué xí Hàn yǔ de rén

chule.en: Besides singing, she can dance too.
chule.why: With 还, the 除了 part is included and there's more.

chule.en: Everyone has been to Beijing except me.
chule.why: 除了 + X + 以外, then the rest with 都.

chule.ch: 除了数学，别的课我喜欢。
chule.fix: 除了数学，别的课我都喜欢。
chule.en: I like every subject except maths.
chule.why: To say "all except", the second half needs 都.

chule.ch: 除了游泳以外，我还喜欢爬山。
chule.en: Apart from swimming, I also like hiking.
chule.why: 除了……还 adds more: swimming, and hiking too.

chule.en: Everyone in my family likes fish except me.
chule.why: 除了 comes right before the one left out, and 以外 closes it.

ruguo.ch: __你明天有时间，我们一起去爬山吧。
ruguo.en: If you're free tomorrow, let's go hiking together.
ruguo.why: 如果 opens the "if" part at the front.

ruguo.en: If you don't feel well, stay at home and rest.
ruguo.why: The "if" part first, then 就 opens the result.

ruguo.ch: 我们就去公园，如果明天天气好。
ruguo.fix: 如果明天天气好，我们就去公园。
ruguo.en: If the weather's good tomorrow, we'll go to the park.
ruguo.why: The "if" part comes first in Chinese.

ruguo.ch: 你饿了的话，冰箱里有面包。
ruguo.en: If you're hungry, there's bread in the fridge.
ruguo.why: 的话 at the end of the first part can mark "if" on its own.

ruguo.en: If you can't find it, give me a call.
ruguo.why: 的话 goes at the end of the "if" part.
ppy: jiù gěi wǒ dǎ diàn huà ba

zhiyao.ch: 只要你努力，__会有好成绩。
zhiyao.en: As long as you work hard, you'll get good results.
As long as I have time, I'll come and see you.
zhiyao.why: 只要 + condition, then subject + 就 + result.

zhiyao.ch: 只要多练习，就你能说好。
zhiyao.fix: 只要多练习，你就能说好。
zhiyao.en: As long as you practise a lot, you'll speak it well.
zhiyao.why: 就 goes after the subject of the second half.

zhiyao.ch: 只要有你在，我就不害怕。
zhiyao.en: As long as you're here, I'm not scared.
zhiyao.why: 只要 names a condition that's enough; 就 comes after 我.

zhiyao.en: Just tell me and I'll definitely help you.
zhiyao.why: 只要 goes before the condition; the subject can come before it.

zhiyou.ch: 只有多听多说，__能说好汉语。
zhiyou.en: Only by listening and speaking a lot will you speak Chinese well.
zhiyou.why: 只有 pairs with 才, not 就.

zhiyou.en: He'll only come if you go.
zhiyou.why: 只有 + the one condition, then subject + 才 + result.

zhiyou.en: It's only possible if the manager agrees.
zhiyou.why: 只有 pairs with 才, not 就.

zhiyou.ch: 只有生病的时候，他才去医院。
zhiyou.en: He only goes to hospital when he's ill.
zhiyou.why: 只有 names the one case; 才 comes before the verb.

zhiyou.en: Only your mum can help you with this.
zhiyou.why: 只有 goes right before the one person who can do it.

yi-ye-bu.en: I haven't spent a single cent today.
yi-ye-bu.why: 一 + measure + 也 + 没有: not even one.
一点儿 comes before 也不, and the adjective goes last.

yi-ye-bu.ch: 这儿的菜一点儿也不贵。
yi-ye-bu.en: The food here isn't expensive at all.
yi-ye-bu.why: 一点儿也不 + adjective means "not at all".

yi-ye-bu.en: He doesn't have a single friend.
yi-ye-bu.why: 一……也 only goes with 不 or 没有.

yi-ye-bu.en: I haven't had a single day off this week.
yi-ye-bu.why: The 一 phrase goes before 也没有 and the verb.

ganxingqu.ch: 我妹妹__画画儿很感兴趣。
ganxingqu.en: My little sister is really interested in drawing.
ganxingqu.why: What you're interested in goes after 对.

ganxingqu.en: Are you interested in Chinese history?
ganxingqu.why: 对 + topic + 感兴趣; the topic never comes after it.

ganxingqu.en: My dad is interested in sport.
ganxingqu.why: The topic goes after 对, before 感兴趣.

ganxingqu.ch: 她对做菜一点儿也不感兴趣。
ganxingqu.en: She isn't the least bit interested in cooking.
ganxingqu.why: 对 + topic, then the 不 part right before 感兴趣.

ganxingqu.en: I'm not very interested in computer games.
ganxingqu.why: 对 comes right before the topic.

guanyu.ch: 他给我讲了一个__北京的故事。
guanyu.en: He told me a story about Beijing.
guanyu.why: 关于 + topic + 的 says what a story is about.

guanyu.en: This is a book about music.
guanyu.why: The 关于 part goes before the noun, joined by 的.

guanyu.ch: 我喜欢看电影关于历史。
guanyu.fix: 我喜欢看关于历史的电影。
guanyu.en: I like watching films about history.
guanyu.why: The 关于 part goes before the noun, with 的.

guanyu.ch: 关于这件事情，你去问经理吧。
guanyu.why: At the start of a sentence, 关于 sets the topic.

guanyu.en: Do you have any books on Chinese culture?
guanyu.why: 关于 goes before the topic, and the topic + 的 before the noun.

dir-simple.why: 来 points towards the speaker, who is upstairs.
The place goes between the verb and 去.
The place goes between the verb and 来 / 去.
回来: back towards home, where Mum is and where I now am.
去 comes right after 出: out, away from here.

dir-compound.en: He took a book out of his bag.
dir-compound.why: 出 gives the direction (out), 来 says towards us; the thing sits between.
Verb + 进 + place + 去: the place goes before the final 去.
The place goes before the final 来.
下 gives the direction; 来 says it's towards us.

dir-compound.en: Please get that book down for me.
dir-compound.why: 下来 goes right after the verb: 拿下来.

dir-extended.ch: 听到这个故事，大家都笑了__。
dir-extended.en: When they heard the story, everyone burst out laughing.
dir-extended.why: 起来 here means something starts, not going up.

dir-extended.en: His health is slowly getting better.
dir-extended.why: 起来 comes right after the adjective: 好起来了.

dir-extended.en: Her face started to go red.
dir-extended.why: 起来 comes after the adjective, not before it.

dir-extended.ch: 我看出来了，你今天不高兴。
dir-extended.en: I can tell you're not happy today.
dir-extended.why: 看出来 means "tell by looking", not moving out.

dir-extended.en: He's started putting on weight lately.
dir-extended.why: 起来 goes after the adjective: 胖起来了.

potential.en: He talks too fast, I can't understand.
potential.why: 不 goes between the verb and its result: 听不懂.

potential.en: Can you finish it on your own?
potential.why: Verb + 得 + result asks whether it can be done: 吃得完.

potential.ch: 这个字太小了，我不能看清楚。
potential.fix: 这个字太小了，我看不清楚。
potential.en: This character is too small, I can't make it out.
potential.why: Put 不 inside: 看不清楚, not 不能看清楚.

potential.ch: 这些题不难，我一个小时做得完。
potential.en: These questions aren't hard, I can get them done in an hour.
potential.why: 做得完: 得 between the verb and the result says it can be done.
不 goes between the verb and its result: 找不到.

de-state.en: She cried so much her eyes went red.
de-state.why: 得 brings in what the crying led to.

de-state.en: I'm so busy I haven't had time for a drink of water.
de-state.why: Adjective + 得 + what it led to.

de-state.en: She was so worried she cried.
de-state.why: No 很 before the word that takes 得.

de-state.ch: 这个电影好看得我看了三次。
de-state.en: This film is so good I've seen it three times.
de-state.why: A whole phrase after 得 shows how good it is.

de-state.en: It's so hot today nobody wants to go out.
de-state.why: 得 comes right after the adjective, then what it led to.

duration.en: He watches two hours of TV every evening.
duration.why: A length of time goes after the verb, before the object.

duration.en: I worked at a bank for five years.
duration.why: How long comes after the verb: 工作了五年.
How long goes after the verb, not before it.

duration.en: He spent the whole afternoon reading.
duration.why: With an object, say the verb twice: 看书看了 + how long.

duration.en: He spent an hour doing his homework.
duration.why: The length goes after the repeated verb: 写了一个小时.

jile.ch: 我找到了新工作，高兴__了！
jile.en: I've found a new job, I'm over the moon!
jile.why: 极了 comes after the word it makes stronger.
Adjective + 极了: as good as it gets.
极了 is already the strongest, so don't add 非常.

jile.en: I'm worn out after a whole day's work.
jile.why: 极了 goes after the adjective, with no 很 or 非常.
极了 goes right after the adjective.

haishi-huozhe.en: Do you want to go to the supermarket or the park?
haishi-huozhe.why: In a question that asks you to choose, use 还是.

haishi-huozhe.ch: 我们可以坐地铁__坐公共汽车去。
haishi-huozhe.en: We can take the underground or the bus.
haishi-huozhe.why: In a statement, "or" is 或者.

haishi-huozhe.en: Would you like rice or noodles?
haishi-huozhe.why: Asking someone to choose takes 还是.

haishi-huozhe.ch: 你是坐地铁去还是坐出租车去？
haishi-huozhe.en: Are you going by underground or by taxi?
haishi-huozhe.why: A choice question with 还是, and no 吗.

haishi-huozhe.en: Every day I go running or swimming.
haishi-huozhe.why: It's a statement, so "or" is 或者, between the two options.

you-zai.ch: 这个电影太好看了，我想__看一次。
you-zai.en: This film is so good, I want to see it again.
you-zai.why: The repeat hasn't happened yet, so it takes 再.

you-zai.ch: 我的手机昨天坏了，今天__坏了。
you-zai.en: My phone broke yesterday, and it's broken again today.
you-zai.why: It has already happened again, so it takes 又.

you-zai.ch: 这里的菜很好吃，我下次又来。
you-zai.fix: 这里的菜很好吃，我下次再来。
you-zai.en: The food here is great, I'll come again next time.
you-zai.why: 下次 is still to come, so use 再.

you-zai.ch: 下个星期又是我的生日了。
you-zai.en: It's my birthday again next week.
you-zai.why: Something that comes round on its own can take 又, even in the future.

you-zai.en: I'm too tired today, let's talk about it tomorrow.
you-zai.why: It hasn't happened yet, so 再 goes right before the verb.
ppy: jīn tiān wǒ tài lèi le

cai-jiu.ch: 我等了他一个小时，他__来。
cai-jiu.en: I waited an hour for him before he finally turned up.
cai-jiu.why: 才 says it happened later than expected.

cai-jiu.ch: 我家离公司很近，走路五分钟__到了。
cai-jiu.en: I live close to the office, it's only five minutes on foot.
cai-jiu.why: 就 + 了 says sooner or easier than expected.

cai-jiu.ch: 电影八点开始，他九点才来了。
cai-jiu.fix: 电影八点开始，他九点才来。
cai-jiu.en: The film started at eight, and he didn't turn up till nine.

cai-jiu.ch: 我妹妹三岁就会游泳了。
cai-jiu.en: My little sister could swim at just three.
cai-jiu.why: 就 + 了: earlier than you'd expect.

cai-jiu.en: This question was hard, it took me an hour to work it out.
cai-jiu.why: 才 goes right before the verb, after how long it took.
ppy: xiǎng le yí ge xiǎo shí

gang.en: What did you just say? I didn't catch it.
gang.why: Only 刚才 can open a sentence.

gang.en: I've just got to the airport, where are you?
gang.why: 刚 goes after the subject, right before the verb.

gang.en: I phoned you a moment ago.
gang.why: 刚 can't open a sentence; use 刚才.

gang.en: He only got married two months ago.
gang.why: 刚 can mean "only recently" over a longer time.

gang.en: The film's just started, hurry in.
gang.why: 刚 goes right before the verb: 刚开始.

hui-guess.why: 会……的 is a confident guess about what will happen.
不会 goes before the verb; 的 at the end makes it sound sure.
The time word comes before 会.

hui-guess.en: Don't worry, you'll get used to it.
hui-guess.why: 会 + verb + 的: a reassuring "you will".

hui-guess.en: Wear a bit more, it'll be cold tonight.
hui-guess.why: 会 goes after the time word, before what you expect.
ppy: duō chuān yì diǎn r ba

adj-redup.en: Her eyes are big and lovely.
adj-redup.why: A one-syllable adjective doubles as AA, with no 很.
The doubled adjective takes 的 at the end.

adj-redup.ch: 这个孩子的脸很红红的。
adj-redup.en: This child's face is all rosy.
adj-redup.why: No 很 with a doubled adjective.
A two-syllable adjective doubles as AABB, then 地 before the verb.

adj-redup.en: Please wash the clothes till they're nice and clean.
adj-redup.why: The doubled adjective comes after 得 and before 的.

verb-abab.en: You should go over things a bit before the test.
verb-abab.why: A two-syllable verb doubles as ABAB, with nothing in between.

verb-abab.en: Let's go to the park and get a bit of exercise.
verb-abab.why: The doubled verb comes after where you go: 运动运动.

verb-abab.en: Have a bit of a rest.
verb-abab.why: No 一 inside a two-syllable verb.

verb-abab.ch: 你给我们介绍介绍你的国家吧。
verb-abab.en: Tell us a bit about your country.
verb-abab.why: 介绍介绍 means introduce a little, casually.

verb-abab.en: Let me look over your homework for you.
verb-abab.why: Verbs double ABAB; AABB is for adjectives.

any-wh.ch: 这个问题太简单了，__都知道。
any-wh.en: This question is so easy, everybody knows it.

any-wh.why: The question word and 也 go before 不 and the verb.
The question word and 都 go before the verb.

any-wh.ch: 他生病了，哪儿都不想去。
any-wh.en: He's ill and doesn't want to go anywhere.
any-wh.why: 哪儿 + 都 + 不 means nowhere.
也 comes right after the question word, before 没有.

neng-rhet.ch: 明天考试，今天我能__复习吗？
neng-rhet.en: There's a test tomorrow, how could I not revise today?
neng-rhet.why: 能不……吗 means "of course I will".

neng-rhet.en: My child still isn't home, how could I not be worried?
neng-rhet.why: The reason comes first, then 能不……吗 to make the point.

neng-rhet.ch: 这个问题很简单，我能不知道吗？
neng-rhet.en: It's an easy question, of course I know!
neng-rhet.why: A negative 能 question means yes: of course I know.

neng-rhet.ch: 朋友生病了，我不去能看他吗？
neng-rhet.fix: 朋友生病了，我能不去看他吗？
neng-rhet.en: My friend is ill, how could I not go and see him?
neng-rhet.why: 不 goes after 能, right before the verb: 能不去……吗.

neng-rhet.en: It's far too expensive, how could I buy it?
neng-rhet.why: A positive 能……吗 here means "no way".

ne-where.en: Where's my umbrella? It was here a moment ago.
ne-where.why: Noun + 呢, with nothing before it, asks where it is.
The thing you're looking for, then 呢.
Use 呢 or 在哪儿, not both.

ne-where.ch: 孩子们呢？他们去公园了吗？
ne-where.en: Where are the kids? Have they gone to the park?
ne-where.why: 孩子们呢 asks where they are.

ne-where.en: Where's the dictionary I left on the table just now?
ne-where.why: 呢 goes at the very end, after the thing you're looking for.

le-change.en: He used to be fat, but he's slim now.
le-change.why: 了 at the end says things have changed.
会 + verb + 了: a new ability.

le-change.en: I'm full now, I won't have any more.
le-change.why: 了 marks the new state: full now, not eating any more.

le-change.ch: 我不在那家公司工作了。
le-change.en: I don't work at that company any more.

le-change.why: 了 at the end marks reaching a new stage.

clock-ban.ch: 现在是三点__，还有十五分钟就四点了。
clock-ban.en: It's a quarter to four, fifteen minutes till four o'clock.
clock-ban.why: 三刻 is three quarters past: 3:45.
Number + 点 + 一刻: a quarter past.

clock-ban.en: They'll get here at quarter past two.
clock-ban.why: Two o'clock is 两点, not 二点.

clock-ban.ch: 现在差五分十二点，我们去吃东西吧。
clock-ban.en: It's five to twelve, let's go and eat.
clock-ban.why: With 差, the minutes come before the hour.

clock-ban.en: Let's meet at half past six at the school gate.
clock-ban.why: 半 comes right after 点.

zuoyou.ch: 我的行李箱有二十公斤__。
zuoyou.en: My suitcase weighs about twenty kilos.
zuoyou.why: 左右 goes after the amount: roughly that much.
左右 comes after the whole amount.

zuoyou.en: Let's set off at around eight.
zuoyou.why: 左右 comes after the amount, not before it.

zuoyou.ch: 他每天晚上十点左右回家。
zuoyou.en: He gets home at around ten every night.
zuoyou.why: Time + 左右: a bit before or a bit after.

zuoyou.en: These leather shoes cost about 300 yuan, not too expensive.
zuoyou.why: 左右 goes right after the amount.

de-de-de.en: This is the food my mum made.
de-de-de.why: 菜 is a noun, so 的.
After the verb 写, how it went takes 得.
Before the verb 看, how it is done takes 地.
After a verb, how it went takes 得.
高兴 says how 回家 was done, before the verb: 地.
